title: Evals regression scoreboard + config-aware alert harmonization (Slack & PagerDuty)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a correlated 'regression scoreboard' in Console that ties quality regressions to specific model/config changes and harmonizes alerts to reduce noise. Key outcomes: (1) surface probable root cause (model revision, quantization profile, routing policy), (2) create a configurable alert-fingerprint + suppression layer so Slack and PagerDuty integrations only surface actionable regressions, (3) provide dashboard widgets for trend, heatmap, and incident provenance for on-call and PMs.
context: We currently get frequent eval-triggered alerts during rollouts and autoscaling changes that are noisy because they lack config-aware grouping and provenance. On-call teams have had multiple ignorable P1s during routine canaries. Existing evals dashboards show deltas but don't attribute to configuration or model hash. This work unifies telemetry (eval signals, config-change events, rollout metadata) in Console and adds a dedupe/aggregation policy for downstream integrations.
success_criteria: Console shows a Regression Scoreboard entry for each significant eval regression with linked change candidates (model hash, quant profile, routing rule)
Slack alerts for regressions are reduced by >=65% in false positives in the first 30 days (based on sampled incidents)
PagerDuty pages for eval regressions are only generated for regressions that pass the aggregated fingerprint + impact rules (configurable per-team)
Teams can annotate and mark regressions as known rollouts to suppress further alerts for the rollout window
Rollout-aware suppression applies automatically during canary and staged rollouts based on rollout metadata
engineering_notes: Plan: add a change-correlator service that consumes eval alerts, config-change events (model_version, quant_profile, routing_policy), and rollout-trace IDs. Produce a single regression event with provenance tags.
Fingerprinting: use (model_hash, config_hash, eval_suite_id, time_bucket) as primary aggregation key with fallbacks to similarity-based clustering for noisy variants.
Suppression window: default 60 minutes for canary rollouts, configurable per-project. Advanced mode: dynamic window proportional to rollout %.
Telemetry: emit regression.score, regression.confidence, candidate_causes list and links to associated PRs and rollouts.

Integration: Slack -> channel threads, with an attach to open Console scoreboard link. PagerDuty -> only trigger when regression.score > threshold AND impacted_tokens_estimate > X. Threshold configurable per team.
qa_plan: Synthetic regressions will be injected in staging by toggling a scoring function and flipping a test model hash. Validate that scoreboard entries appear, Slack shows a single aggregated message, and PagerDuty is suppressed when configured. Run end-to-end with sample canary rollout metadata present.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: opt-in beta for infra and platform teams (2 weeks). Phase 2: expand to all internal teams with configurable defaults (2 weeks). Phase 3: enable as default but allow project-level overrides. Monitor false positive rate and pages metrics for 30 days post-default-enable.
acceptance_criteria: Merged Console UI + correlator service, Slack and PagerDuty integrations wired with config UI for suppression thresholds, documented runbook and toggle in admin settings, and observed reduction in noise in staging tests.
